_about: Facts an on-call engineer would give when the Parser asks a question. The benchmark answers every question for a runbook with its notes, standing in for the person typing answers in the web app.
restart-web-service.md: The script runs directly on the affected server, so no SSH step is needed. To clear old logs, delete *.gz and *.1 rotated files older than 7 days under /var/log/nginx only. 'Looks OK' means nginx is active and the health page returns 200. The ticket is updated by hand, outside the script.
clear-disk-space.md: The script runs on the server itself. 'Older than 7 days' means file modification time (find -mtime +7); older than 2 days means -mtime +2. Never touch access.log, error.log or any uncompressed current log. Usage going down OR staying the same is fine. The ticket note is done by hand.
check-ssl-certificate.md: Days left = (expiry date - today) in whole days, using date -d. The script only reports: it exits 0 for OK and WARNING, and exits non-zero only if the certificate file is missing or already expired. Key permissions 600 or 400 are acceptable.
collect-diagnostics.md: Use hostname and today's date as YYYYMMDD in the folder name. If a log file is missing, write a note into the bundle instead of failing. Attaching to the ticket is done by hand; the script just prints the archive path and size.
daily-health-check.md: Reasonable load means the 1-minute load average is below 2x the number of CPUs (nproc); report it as WARN otherwise, not FAIL. Disk over 85% and low memory are WARN. Only a stopped service or a health page not returning 200 is FAIL. Counting [crit] lines is informational only.
clear-app-cache.md: Use 'systemctl status myapp' to check it is running; if it is not running, continue anyway and start it at the end. 'Nearly empty' means zero files left in the two cache folders. Escalation is done by hand: the script fails with a clear message if health is not 200 within 30 seconds.
fix-web-permissions.md: The uploads folder /var/www/html/uploads must stay owned by www-data with mode 755 so the web server (running as www-data) can write to it; do not make it world-writable. The site check passes when curl http://localhost/ returns 200.
onboard-linux-user.md: For this ticket: username jdoe, full name Jane Doe, public key 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHbK4m2q9u6yQd0dQ0v7cJ2X1o5N3wQ2l8b9T0f1R2s3 jdoe@laptop'. A public key is not a secret, so it may appear in the script; pass username, full name and key as variables at the top. Lock the password with 'passwd -l' or create the user without one. The ticket update is done by hand.
change-nginx-upload-limit.md: The default site file has a single server block. Use a timestamp like YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS in the backup name. In dry-run mode, only report what would change; the real edit, test and reload happen with --execute. Use sed or awk to edit the file, never an interactive editor.
restart-app-after-crash.md: Count lines containing 'out of memory' or 'OOM' (case-insensitive). Try the health page up to 10 times, 1 second apart. Escalation is done by hand; the script exits non-zero with the last 20 log lines printed if the app does not come back. The nginx front end check means http://localhost/health returns 200.
